title: Breaking the sound barrier
text: On October 14, 1947, over what is now Edwards Air Force Base, Captain Chuck Yeager became the first person to fly faster than the speed of sound. He flew a Bell XS-1 nicknamed Glamorous Glennis, and a sonic boom was heard across the Mojave Desert. The flight was over Rogers Dry Lake, a dry lakebed so flat that it could serve as a giant runway. Back then the base was called Muroc, a reversal of Corum, because California already had a town named Coram. It was later renamed for Captain Glen Edwards, who died in 1948 in the crash of a Northrop YB-49 flying wing.
